article_title: Confirming Correct, Missing the Rest: LLM Tutoring Agents Struggle Where Feedback Matters Most
citation: Tahreem Yasir, Wenbo Li, Sam Gilson, Sutapa Dey Tithi, Xiaoyi Tian, Tiffany Barnes. (2026). Confirming Correct, Missing the Rest: LLM Tutoring Agents Struggle Where Feedback Matters Most. arXiv:2605.16207. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16207
title: KG-grounded benchmark of 10,836 solution-feedback pairs for step-level LLM tutoring evaluation
description: The article introduces what it calls "the first benchmark for step-level evaluation of LLM tutoring feedback across multiple valid solution paths." It is built from 516 unique proof states drawn from 32 proof problems across five practice levels of a propositional logic tutor deployed in an undergraduate Discrete Mathematics course, with LLM-simulated next-step solutions and reasoning traces. The article reports that "we evaluate 10,836 LLM- simulated next-step solutions and their feedback with KG-grounded evaluation across seven mod- els and three feedback conditions." Code and data are released in a public repository.
requirements: LLM-simulated student solutions with reasoning traces, because the tutoring system logs lack reasoning traces needed for step-level reasoning evaluation
constraints: Proof states come from a single undergraduate Discrete Mathematics course at one institution, which the authors state limits the diversity of reasoning contexts and problem types
target_learning_goals: step-level propositional logic proof diagnosis and feedback evaluation
examples: Each of seven models served as both student simulator generating solutions for all 516 proof states and feedback agent evaluating all solutions under three conditions
key_sources: Tahreem Yasir, Wenbo Li, Sam Gilson, Sutapa Dey Tithi, Xiaoyi Tian, Tiffany Barnes. (2026). Confirming Correct, Missing the Rest: LLM Tutoring Agents Struggle Where Feedback Matters Most. arXiv:2605.16207. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16207

article_title: Multi-source Education Knowledge Graph Construction and Fusion for College Curricula
citation: Zeju Li, Linya Cheng, Chunhong Zhang, Xinning Zhu, Hui Zhao. (2023). Multi-source Education Knowledge Graph Construction and Fusion for College Curricula. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.04567
title: Four-part knowledge graph fusion preserving hierarchy, attributes and edges
description: The article's fusion method integrates fragmentary nodes referring to the same knowledge concept across sources while retaining information content. It proceeds in four parts: "entity name matching, locating coarse-grained entities, attribute union, and preserving original edges". The fused node is placed at the coarsest granularity level, attributes (except url) are unioned, and all pre-fusion connection relationships are reconnected to the unique fused node. Fusion is applied both within a course across sources and between courses.
requirements: Entity name matching using string matching, literal similarity and semantic similarity to determine whether entities refer to the same concept
constraints: The fused node is located at the coarsest level of the entities fused, which the authors state preserves the hierarchical structure
target_learning_goals: integrating distributed knowledge concepts into a unified knowledge base
examples: Two 'anti-noise performance' nodes were fused into one node retaining the union of name, description, word frequency and ranker attributes
key_sources: Zeju Li, Linya Cheng, Chunhong Zhang, Xinning Zhu, Hui Zhao. (2023). Multi-source Education Knowledge Graph Construction and Fusion for College Curricula. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.04567

article_title: Towards Sustainable Learning in Online Education: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
citation: Chaofan Zhai, Yicheng Song, Ravi Bapna, Junyao Ye. (2025). Towards Sustainable Learning in Online Education: A Reinforcement Learning Approach. https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Towards+Sustainable+Learning+in+Online+Education+A+Reinforcement+Learning+Approach
title: Knowledge-graph-based action-space masking for developmentally appropriate recommendations
description: At each step, the feasible action space is restricted using the learner's learned subgraph: adjacent nodes represent new items directly connected to previously learned content, and nodes within the subgraph represent previously learned items available for review. The article states this masking "optimizes exploration and ensures that all recommended knowledge items are developmentally appropriate", operationalizing constructivist learning theory by keeping new material just beyond the learner's knowledge boundary.
requirements: A constructed knowledge graph and the learner's current learning-path subgraph to induce adjacency
constraints: Unconstrained action space over the full knowledge pool leads to inefficient exploration, higher computational cost, and risk of recommending content far beyond the learner's level
target_learners: Learners progressing through structured course knowledge pools
target_learning_goals: Balancing new knowledge acquisition with review of prior items
examples: The allowable action set at time t includes both adjacent new nodes and internal review nodes of subgraph g_t
key_sources: Chaofan Zhai, Yicheng Song, Ravi Bapna, Junyao Ye. (2025). Towards Sustainable Learning in Online Education: A Reinforcement Learning Approach. https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=Towards+Sustainable+Learning+in+Online+Education+A+Reinforcement+Learning+Approach

article_title: HIV/AIDS Infected Mothers' Experience of a Group Intervention to Enhance Their Children's Behavior
citation: Irma Eloff and Michelle Finestone; Brian Forsyth. (2016). HIV/AIDS infected mothers’ experience of a group intervention to enhance their children’s behavior. South African Journal of Education, Volume 36, Number 2. https://doi.org/10.15700/saje.v36n2a1285
title: Kgolo Mmogo culturally tailored support group intervention and open-access manual
description: The Kgolo Mmogo intervention is a six-month, theory-based support group programme in which HIV-positive mothers and their 6–10-year-old children attend weekly small-group sessions. "The mothers and children attended 14 separate sessions and 10 joint sessions." The child sessions followed "a manual that was culturally tailored and focused on coping, problem -solving, emotional intelligence, social skills , and a positive future orientation", while mother sessions focused on coping with the HIV diagnosis, parenting skills and child development. The manual is "an open access resource" available online, and groups were facilitated by trained community care workers receiving weekly supervision from a psychologist and social worker.
requirements: Facilitation by community care workers who received intensive training and weekly supervision from a psychologist and social worker, and who were proficient in the children's languages (Sepedi, Setswana, Isizulu and Sesotho).
constraints: Developed specifically to be age appropriate for children 6–10 years old in the South African Tshwane context.
target_learners: Latency-phase children aged 6–10 years affected by maternal HIV/AIDS
HIV-positive mothers in low-income South African communities
examples: 12 groups or waves of mothers and children participated, with on average eight participants per wave attending the support groups.
key_sources: Irma Eloff and Michelle Finestone; Brian Forsyth. (2016). HIV/AIDS infected mothers’ experience of a group intervention to enhance their children’s behavior. South African Journal of Education, Volume 36, Number 2. https://doi.org/10.15700/saje.v36n2a1285
